# Cacio e Pepe

## Ingredients

- 200 g tonnarelli
- 100 g pecorino romano, very finely grated
- 2 tsp black pepper, cracked and toasted
- salt

## Steps

1. Crack the black pepper coarsely and toast it in a dry pan until it smells sharp and warm.
2. Boil the tonnarelli in as little water as I can get away with so it stays properly starchy. Save a mug of the pasta water.
3. Off the heat, work the pecorino romano with a few spoons of the starchy pasta water into a smooth paste. This emulsifying step is everything, it must happen away from any flame.
4. Drain the pasta, add it to the cheese mix off the heat, and toss hard, adding starchy water a splash at a time until the sauce coats every strand.
5. Fold in the toasted cracked black pepper and serve at once in warm bowls.

The sauce tightens as it cools, so I keep a little warm water to loosen each portion. If the cheese clumps, the pan was too hot. Grate the pecorino on the finest setting you own, a coarse grate will never melt smoothly. I use a deep bowl and a wooden spoon, because the mix needs room to move. The whole thing takes eleven minutes once the water boils, so I get the cheese and pepper ready before the tonnarelli goes in. A final grind of black pepper over the bowl is the last thing I do.
